intro: Everything you have met in the verses, gathered into one reference. Each rule links to a verse where it appears.

sections.title: Sandhi: how sounds join
sections.html:
When words meet, their sounds change. These are the rules you have met on this site, with a verse for each.

Vowel sandhi

RuleExampleSeen in
Same vowels merge (savarna dirgha): अ/आ + अ/आ → आदृष्ट्वा + अहिम् → दृष्ट्वाहिम्Peacock
Guna: अ + इ → ए, अ + उ → ओशिव + इति → शिवेति · तस्य + उपरि → तस्योपरिTandava 13
Vriddhi: अ + ए → ऐ, अ + ओ → औसदा + एव → सदैव · दुःख + ओघ → दुःखौघRudrashtakam 8
Yan: इ → य्, उ → व् before a different vowelहस्तेषु + अङ्ग → हस्तेष्वङ्गBamboo
Avagraha: ए/ओ + अ → ए/ओ + ऽशिवः + अहम् → शिवोऽहम्Nirvana 1

Visarga sandhi

Beforeः becomesExample
त, थस्हारः + तारः → हारस्तारः
च, छश्भागाः + च → भागाश्च
a voiced sound, after -अ-ओविशीर्णः + भूमौ → विशीर्णो भूमौ
a voiced sound, after other vowelsर्शम्भोः + हरेः → शम्भोर्हरेः
अ, after -अ-ओ + ऽअंशः + अस्य → अंशोऽस्य

Consonant sandhi

ChangeExample
त् → द् before a vowel or voiced soundतोयात् + ऊर्ध्वम् → तोयादूर्ध्वम्
त् → न् before a nasalनमत् + निलिम्प → नमन्निलिम्प
त् → ल् before लज्वलत् + ललाट → ज्वलल्ललाट
त् → ज् before जजगत् + जय → जगज्जय
त् + श → च्छपठेत् + शिव → पठेच्छिव
छ doubles after a short vowelस्मर + छिद् → स्मरच्छिद्
न → ण after र, ष in the same wordप्र + नमामि → प्रणमामि

sections.title: The eight cases (vibhakti)
sections.html:
A Sanskrit noun changes its ending to show its role. Here are the eight cases with examples from the verses.

CaseQuestionExampleVerse
1. Nominative (prathama)who? (subject)शिवः Shiva (does)Tandava 1
2. Accusative (dvitiya)whom? where to?मालतीम् to the jasmineBees
3. Instrumental (tritiya)by / with what?अनिलेन by the windLotus
4. Dative (chaturthi)for whom? for what?श्रियै for prosperityTandava 5
5. Ablative (panchami)from where? because of?बिलात् from the holePeacock
6. Genitive (shashthi)whose? of what?शम्भोः of ShambhuVishnu
7. Locative (saptami)where? when? in what?निशि at nightBees
8. Vocative (sambodhana)calling someoneबाले O girl!Verse 1

Sanskrit also has three numbers: singular, dual (exactly two) and plural. See the six duals in Tandava 12: तल्पयोः, स्रजोः, लोष्ठयोः…

sections.title: Compounds (samasa)
sections.html:
Sanskrit joins words into long compounds. Only the last word takes a case ending.

TypeHow it worksExample
TatpurushaX of Y; the last word is the headअलिसंख्या number of bees
DvandvaX and Y (and Z…)केतकमालती ketaki and jasmine; पाशाङ्कुश…शूलैः
Bahuvrihidescribes something else: 'one whose …'मधुव्रत 'whose vow is honey' = bee; चन्द्रशेखर
Upapadanoun + verbal root as 'doer'सरोज lake-born; स्मरच्छिद् Kama-chutter
Avyayibhavaadverb compoundप्रतिक्षणम् every moment
nir- / a- negationwithout / notनिराकार, निर्गुण, अचल, अखण्ड

sections.title: Meter (chandas)
sections.html:
Laghu (light, ◡, 1 matra): a short vowel followed by at most one consonant. Guru (heavy, —, 2 matras): a long vowel (आ ई ऊ ए ऐ ओ औ), or any vowel followed by ं, ः or two consonants. The last syllable of a line may be either.

The eight ganas

Syllables are grouped in threes. The memory word यमाताराजभानसलगा (ya-ma-ta-ra-ja-bha-na-sa-la-ga) encodes them: start at any syllable and read three.

GanaPatternGanaPattern
ya◡ — —ja◡ — ◡
ma— — —bha— ◡ ◡
ta— — ◡na◡ ◡ ◡
ra— ◡ —sa◡ ◡ —

sections.title: Word numerals (bhuta-sankhya)
sections.html:
Mathematicians wrote numbers as words for things that come in that number, so numbers could fit the meter. Digits are read right to left: अङ्कानां वामतो गतिः. So पञ्च-त्रि-एक = 135 (verse 8).

NumberWordsWhy
1चन्द्र, शशिन्, भूone moon, one earth
2नेत्र, नयन, कर, पक्षtwo eyes, two hands
3गुण, राम, अग्निthree gunas, three Ramas, three sacred fires
4वेद, युग, समुद्रfour Vedas, four ages, four oceans
5बाण, इषु, भूतKama's five arrows, five elements
6रस, अङ्ग, ऋतुsix tastes, six Vedangas, six seasons
7मुनि, अश्व, स्वरseven sages, seven horses of the sun, seven notes
8वसु, गज, नागeight Vasus, eight elephants of the directions
9अङ्क, ग्रह, नन्दnine digits, nine planets
10दिश्, अङ्गुलिten directions, ten fingers
11रुद्रeleven Rudras
12सूर्य, दिवाकर, आदित्य, राशिtwelve Adityas, twelve signs
16नृप, भूप, कलाsixteen kings; sixteen digits of the moon
